project.objective: When and where did Kenneth Werner Quass die?

questions.question: When and where did Kenneth Werner Quass, born 4 December 1917 in Sumner, Bremer County, Iowa, son of Ralph Kennedy Quass and Emma Wilhelmina Nehls, die?
questions.rationale: Single event objective (death date and place) for the subject KNS4-P6W. The tree holds no death fact. The last dated residence is Marshall, Minnesota (1940) and a move to Los Angeles, California is dated 2 July 1962, so the death could fall in either place. Two uploaded captures (a Find a Grave memorial and a Texas death certificate) are present and not yet read; they are for later research to use, not evidence yet.

search_stop.justification: Overturn risk: high. The place and date of death are not established. The only dated death record for the subject's name in Texas (Texas Death Index, record VZZJ-TBB, Kenneth Quass, died 17 Sep 1982, Tarrant County) is an unlinked candidate (h_001; person-evidence declined, same_person 0.35). Its certificate image was never read: the Ancestry capture is an index page, and the uploaded PDF was not re-read as text in this pass. The Find a Grave memorial (QVK1-PM77, linked to KNS4-P6W) shares the 17 Sep 1982 date but gives a Madelia, Minnesota burial and a contributor note disputing the Texas place (death on a Miami-to-San Diego flight, landed at Dallas). That dispute is not extracted or resolved. Wrap-up stop on pl_001: pli_001, pli_002, pli_004, pli_005, pli_006 and pli_012 are completed; pli_003, pli_013 and pli_010 are skipped as fallbacks never triggered; pli_007 and pli_009 are skipped for no coverage and a declined request; pli_011 is skipped as out of scope. Not searched: (1) the readable Texas death certificate image, which would give parents, birth date, informant and place of death (Texas Deaths 1977-1986 and 1890-1977 image sets; the Bureau of Vital Statistics order is paid); (2) Texas residence before 1982, by city directory, Texas census or Texas obituaries (GenealogyBank); (3) an obituary or SSDI entry with the middle name Werner and birth date 4 Dec 1917 (the two SSDI name searches, log_007 and log_008, returned no Kenneth Werner Quass, which is unexplained and does not settle the identity); (4) Minnesota: Madelia and Watonwan County burial and death records for the Riverside Cemetery burial, which have no kept locality and were never planned, and the Lyon County courthouse request (pli_009, declined by the researcher); (5) Los Angeles County death records and cemetery files (Evergreen, Rose Hills), since the California Death Index pool was only partly read (log_001) and no California entry was found by the principal-only search (log_011). These unsearched sources can change the answer; the accessible evidence does not support a defensible place of death. Stop recorded under wrap-up, with no recommendation.

hypotheses.notes: Candidate identity, not adopted. Starts active; no promotion or elimination made. Candidate-side evidence: a_003 (Texas death 17 Sep 1982, primary quality, certifying official, Tarrant, Texas) and a_001/a_002 (name 'Kenneth Quass' and sex male; secondary quality, reported by a family survivor, not witnessed; the record gives no middle name and no birth date, so the given name agrees only partly with 'Kenneth Werner'). Subject-side evidence: a_007 gives the same death date, 17 Sep 1982, but it comes from the Find a Grave index (src_002, indeterminate quality, no informant) which is linked to the subject (pe_004), so the date match is shared by both records and is not independent support for the Texas candidate on its own. Contradicting-side tension (not refutation): a_006 places the subject's burial at Madelia, Watonwan, Minnesota in 1982; a Texas death followed by a Minnesota burial is possible but needs a transport or family-return explanation that the project does not yet document. Person-evidence declined to link the Texas entry to the subject (same_person score 0.35); no birth date on the Texas record, no bridge between Texas and the subject's Minnesota or Iowa residences in the project. Find a Grave memorial's Texas death place is NOT yet extracted as an assertion in the project and is therefore not weighed here; a contributor note disputes it and that dispute is unresolved. Unstated assumption to watch: that two records sharing a death date and surname describe one man. Evidence that would settle it: (1) a readable Texas death certificate showing parents (Ralph Quass / Emma Nehls), birth date or birthplace, and informant; (2) evidence of a Texas residence before 1982 (city directory, census, employment or Social Security earnings in Texas); (3) an obituary or Social Security Death Index entry giving the middle name Werner and birth date 4 December 1917; (4) the Find a Grave Texas death place source and contributor note, extracted and weighed.

proof_summaries.narrative_markdown:
## Question
When and where did Kenneth Werner Quass (KNS4-P6W), born 4 December 1917 in Sumner, Bremer County, Iowa, son of Ralph Kennedy Quass and Emma Wilhelmina Nehls, die?

## Answer in brief
The evidence points to a death on 17 September 1982, but only as a possible answer. The place of death is not established (not proved). This is a wrap-up conclusion, written while important records remain unsearched.

## Date: possible
The Find a Grave Index entry for Kenneth Werner Quass, Sr ("Find a Grave Index", FamilySearch, record ark:/61903/1:1:QVK1-PM77) gives a death of 17 Sep 1982, birth 04 Dec 1917 and burial at Madelia, Watonwan, Minnesota. It is a derivative index of indeterminate quality: it names no informant and the birth is inferred. It is linked to the subject with confidence (exact full name, birth date gap of 0 years, same-person score 0.958), so it is the only record tied to the subject's identity. The Texas Death Index entry ("Texas, Death Index, 1903-2000", record ark:/61903/1:1:VZZJ-TBB) gives Kenneth Quass, male, died 17 Sep 1982, Tarrant, Texas, and its death fact is primary information from a certifying official. Two sources agreeing on a date would normally strengthen it, but the Texas entry is not linked to the subject (same-person score 0.35: no middle name, no birth date, no parents). Its date agreement therefore cannot be counted as independent support, and the subject's date rests on one index of indeterminate quality. The coincidence of surname, given name and exact date is suggestive, which is why the date is possible rather than not proved.

## Place: not proved
Three leads name Tarrant County, Texas: the Texas index entry, the Find a Grave memorial and an uploaded Ancestry index capture. The linked Find a Grave index entry supplies only a Minnesota burial (Madelia), which is a burial place and not a place of death. A contributor note on the memorial says the Texas place is false, describing a death on a Miami-to-San Diego flight that landed at Dallas, with burial in Madelia. That note is unsourced and has not been extracted or weighed as evidence. The uploaded memorial and certificate captures were not read as evidence. A Texas death followed by a Minnesota burial is plausible but undocumented. No place of death is concluded and nothing is written to the tree for it.

## Open candidate h_001
Hypothesis h_001 (active, not adopted) asks whether the Kenneth Quass of the Texas index is the subject. It is unresolved. It would be settled by: (1) the readable Texas death certificate showing parents (Ralph Quass and Emma Nehls), birth date or birthplace and informant; (2) a Texas residence before 1982; (3) an obituary or Social Security record giving the middle name Werner and birth date 4 December 1917; (4) the Find a Grave Texas-place source and contributor note, extracted and weighed. Minnesota death or burial records at Madelia or Watonwan County, and Los Angeles County records (the subject was in Los Angeles in 1962), could independently establish the place. No conflict is registered; the disagreement over place is an unresolved candidate question, not an adjudicated conflict.

## Tree
The tree already carries Death F2 (17 Sep 1982, from the Find a Grave Index, source S2) and Burial F1 (Madelia, Minnesota). No place of death and no Texas fact is encoded. These are evidence facts, not a concluded proof.

## Limits
The unsearched records listed in the search summary can change this answer; the finding is possible, not settled.

quirks: No tool result places Kenneth Werner Quass's death in Marshall or anywhere else; this guide lists where a death record for Marshall would be held, not a confirmed place of death.

Marshall, Lyon County, Minnesota is a different place from Marshall County, Minnesota (a separate county). The survey's county-page sections came from Marshall County, Minnesota Genealogy; do not apply that county's records to Marshall in Lyon County.

The Lyon County Courthouse Clerk of District Court holds birth and death records from 1874 (per the Lyon County Genealogy wiki page), so the county series is the first place to search for a Marshall death.
The FamilySearch Minnesota death collections are statewide and are index-only or index-and-image; their entries give the county and do not by themselves establish a place of death.
The Lyon County cemetery volumes returned by the survey cover Custer, Amiret, Eidsvold, Coon Creek and Grandview townships, not the city of Marshall; do not treat them as Marshall cemetery records.

The Calvary Cemetery church-records microfilm (catalog koha:390369) is catalogued under Marshall, Minnesota; the survey did not confirm the denomination or parish that kept its register, so treat the parish affiliation as unconfirmed.
The Marshall city obituary volumes (1985) are name-indexed but not full-text searchable; they must be browsed by name once located in the index.

The survey returned no Marshall-specific death series for 1940-2024 beyond the statewide collections and the Lyon County courthouse series; a post-1955 Marshall death may need a direct request to the county or the state.

# Locality Guide: Marshall, Lyon, Minnesota, United States (1940-2024)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Lyon County organized March 9, 1875, from Redwood County (per the Lyon County wiki page); Marshall is its county seat (FamilySearch place dates from +1870).
- **County seat / administrative center:** Marshall, Lyon County.
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Minnesota, United States.
- **Population during period:** The survey returned only statewide totals (Minnesota about 2.8 million in 1940 and 4.9 million in 2000); no Marshall or Lyon County figures were returned.
- **Economy:** Not confirmed by this survey.
- **Ethnic composition:** Not confirmed by this survey.
- **Religious denominations:** Calvary Cemetery (Marshall) church records and a St. Paul's Icelandic Lutheran Church series (Minneota) appear in the catalog; the Marshall congregations are not otherwise confirmed.
- **Key historical events:** Not confirmed by this survey.
- **Coverage of this survey:** Marshall has 6 digitized volumes, all listed (total 6, complete); Lyon County as a whole has 82 volumes, of which the survey listed the first page only.

## Boundary changes
- Lyon County was organized March 9, 1875, out of Redwood County (per the Lyon County wiki page). The survey returned no later boundary change for Lyon County or for Marshall.
- Marshall, Lyon County is not Marshall County, Minnesota; the two are separate places.
- The survey did not confirm any boundary change affecting the Marshall records themselves.

## Research tips
- **Search order:** Start with the Lyon County Clerk of District Court, which holds birth and death records from 1874 (per [Lyon County, Minnesota Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Lyon_County,_Minnesota_Genealogy)), then the statewide FamilySearch indexes: Minnesota Death Index 1908-2002 (collection 1937234), Minnesota Deaths 1887-2001 (3398461), and Minnesota Death Records and Certificates 1900-1955 (2477957). Then check the Marshall obituaries: the 1985 volumes and obituary indexes 1873-1953 on FamilySearch, which are name-indexed but not full-text searchable. Browse-only or offline sources come last.
- Minnesota's statewide death indexes are free to search on FamilySearch, but index entries do not themselves establish a place of death; confirm the death place from the certificate or an obituary.
- **Obituaries:** The Minnesota Obituaries 1865-2006 collection (2469546) is on FamilySearch; the Southwest Minnesota Historical Center obituary file index (catalog 408979), Southwest State University obituary files (409008), and Prairieland Genealogical Society obituary files (1197876) and index cards (1197864) are offline, catalogued for Marshall, Minnesota ([Marshall County, Minnesota Genealogy, Obituaries](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Marshall_County,_Minnesota_Genealogy#Obituaries)). Note this wiki page is for Marshall County; the catalog entries name Marshall, Minnesota in Lyon County.
- **Cemetery:** The Marshall Cemetery alphabetized index (catalog koha:525977, FamilySearch Library) is a typescript, about 1992; its three numeric columns are unexplained. The Calvary Cemetery records microfilm (catalog koha:390369) includes death entries 1898-1925 and cemetery records ca. 1900-1990; it is at the FamilySearch Library, Granite Mountain Record Vault (storage), and online at FamilySearch Centers and affiliate libraries.
- **Church records:** Minnesota church records are incomplete online ([Minnesota Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Minnesota_Church_Records)); the parish or denomination for Calvary is unconfirmed.
- **Alternative sources:** Veterans Grave Registration Reports 1930-1975 (4489446) apply only if the decedent was a veteran. Minnesota Will Records 1849-1985 (1607922) may hold a probate file.
- **Finding aids:** Lyon County Courthouse, 607 W Main St, Marshall MN 56258, phone 507-537-6734, with the county website at http://www.lyonco.org/. A negative online result is not absence: the record may be undigitized, unindexed, or held only at the courthouse.

# Locality Guide: Texas, United States (state-level death records) (1962-2024)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Texas was admitted to the Union on 29 December 1845 as the 28th state, created from the Republic of Texas (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Texas,_United_States_Genealogy)
- **County seat / administrative center:** Austin (state capital; same source)
- **Parent jurisdiction:** United States
- **Population during period:** United States figures only were returned by the survey (345,426,571 in 2024; 186,724,272 in 1962); no Texas-only population figure was returned
- **Economy:** not confirmed by this survey
- **Ethnic composition:** not confirmed by this survey
- **Religious denominations:** not confirmed by this survey beyond the Texas Church Records page
- **Key historical events:** not confirmed by this survey
- **Coverage of this survey:** The volumes lookup timed out on both attempts, so no digitized-volume counts are reported. The Catalog returned 10,070 hits for Texas, most of them local histories and family histories rather than death series; no Texas death-register catalog entry was read in this survey.

## Boundary changes
- Texas's boundaries were not reported as changed during 1962-2024 by any tool result in this survey; the state was admitted in 1845 and is the same jurisdiction for the whole period.
- Statewide death registration is the relevant administrative change: the Texas Vital Records page states it began in 1903 with the formation of the Texas Department of Public Health (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Texas_Vital_Records). The Texas Research Tips page gives 1908 for statewide registration (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Texas_Research_Tips_and_Strategies). The two Wiki pages disagree; both are reported.
- Before statewide registration, some cities and towns authorized local registration as early as 1873, per the Research Tips page. Those town series are not named by this survey.

## Research tips
- **Search order:** Start with FamilySearch's Texas Death Index, 1964-1998 (collection 1375599; index only, free), since it is the only listed index that covers the period from 1964. Then search Texas Deaths, 1977-1986 (collection 1930157; index and images, free), and Texas Death Index, 1903-2000 (collection 1949337; index only, free) to cover the whole period. Texas Deaths, 1890-1977 (collection 1983324) and Texas Deaths and Burials, 1903-1973 (collection 1681049) overlap the early years of the period and are free on FamilySearch.
- **Gap at the start of the period:** the name indexes begin in 1964 and the image collections end in 1977 or 1986. Deaths in 1962-1963 are not covered by the listed index; check the image collection 1983324 and then the Bureau of Vital Statistics.
- **Gap after 1986 for images:** the survey listed no FamilySearch death image collection covering 1987-2024. For deaths after 1998 the survey returned only the 1903-2000 index and Ancestry's subscription collections; for an image, order the certificate from the state (http://www.dshs.state.tx.us/vs/default.shtm), which the Texas Vital Records page directs requesters to (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Texas_Vital_Records).
- **Jurisdiction-specific advice:** The Texas Research Tips page notes that death records from 1903 onward asked for the deceased's birth and parent information, though accuracy depended on relatives' memory (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Texas_Research_Tips_and_Strategies).
- **Naming conventions:** The United States Naming Customs page returned only links to abbreviation and name-variation guides, so no Texas-specific naming practice was confirmed (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/United_States_Naming_Customs).
- **Alternative sources when primary records are missing:** obituaries, church records (incomplete; Texas, Church Records, 1852-1994, collection 2790180), cemetery interment cards for Dallas County (collection 3656813) and Harris County Hollywood Cemetery records (collection 2040173). Cite the county-level cemetery sets only for their named counties.
- **Finding aids:** the Texas Record Finder and the Guided Research page for Texas births, marriages and deaths are named on the Texas Research Tips page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Texas_Research_Tips_and_Strategies).
- **Place-of-death check:** The survey cannot confirm the county or city of death for the uploaded Texas death certificate capture. Its place must be read from the capture itself before any county series is searched.

The California Death Index, 1940-1997 is the statewide index that spans the whole 1962 move window; an index entry gives a year and county, and the survey did not confirm that the certificate itself is online.

The Los Angeles City death index (catalog 1173324) covers 1877-1962 and the Los Angeles City death records volume covers 1930-1963; both end at or near the 2 July 1962 move date, so a death later in 1962 may fall outside them.

The Southern California Genealogical Society's Los Angeles Times Obituary Index covers only 1988 to 2004, with some gaps, so it does not reach 1962-1987; copies of obituaries must be bought from the Society.

The survey's volume summary counts 1,709 Death-group volumes for Los Angeles, of which 255 are browse-only and 1,091 full-text searchable; browse-only volumes must be read image by image with no name search.
The Los Angeles County wiki lists neighbouring counties Kern, Orange, San Bernardino and Ventura; search those counties too, since a death near a county line may be filed across it.
The FamilySearch Wiki's California Online Genealogy Records and Research Tips pages returned no body text in this survey, so no claim about them is made here.
The survey does not establish where Kenneth Werner Quass died; the Find a Grave capture and the Texas death certificate capture are not treated as the place of death in this guide.

# Locality Guide: Los Angeles County, California (1962-2024)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** 18 February 1850 as one of the 27 original California counties (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Los_Angeles_County,_California_Genealogy)
- **County seat / administrative center:** Los Angeles
- **Parent jurisdiction:** California, United States
- **Population during period:** California state totals from the survey: 186,724,272 (1962) to 345,426,571 (2024); the survey gave no county-level figures for this period.
- **Economy:** not confirmed by this survey.
- **Ethnic composition:** not confirmed by this survey beyond the county wiki's note on Hispanic and Asian American history.
- **Religious denominations:** the county wiki names Baptist and Lutheran church records only in part; the survey did not confirm the denominations present.
- **Key historical events:** none affecting records is stated in a tool result for this period.
- **Coverage of this survey:** the Los Angeles volume summary is complete at 1,801 volumes; the survey lists only a few of them. Of those, 1,709 are Death-group, 255 of them browse-only.

## Boundary changes
- The original County of Los Angeles covered parts of what are now Kern, San Bernardino, Riverside and Orange counties. San Bernardino County split off in 1853, Kern in 1866, and Orange in 1889; in 1893 part of San Bernardino County that had been Los Angeles territory became part of Riverside County (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Los_Angeles_County,_California_Genealogy).
- Before the county existed, the records were at city or Franciscan mission places (same page, Boundary Changes).
- For a 1962-2024 death in Los Angeles County, the county boundary itself is stable in the sources read; the 1850s-1890s changes do not bear on this period.

## Research tips
- **Search order:** Start with the California Death Index, 1940-1997 (FamilySearch collection 2015582), the only indexed statewide death source that spans the whole 1962 move window; it gives a year and county to test against the move date. Next, the Los Angeles City death index and records (catalog 1173324, 1877-1962 and 1930-1963), then the cemetery and mortuary files, and then the browse-only volumes last (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Los_Angeles_County,_California_Genealogy).
- **Statewide and county series:** Statewide registration of deaths began in 1905, and the county's death dates begin in 1874. The County Recorder holds death records at Hall of Records, 320 W. Temple Street (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Los_Angeles_County,_California_Genealogy; https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/California_Vital_Records).
- **Obituaries:** The Los Angeles Times Obituary Index (Southern California Genealogical Society) covers 1988-2004 only, so it does not reach 1962-1987; copies must be bought from the Society (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Los_Angeles_County,_California_Genealogy#Obituaries).
- **Cemeteries and mortuaries:** Angelus-Rosedale Cemetery/Crematory Records 1884-2002 (collection 3583819), Evergreen Memorial Park deceased card file 1877-1989 (collection 3259479), Pierce Brothers Cunningham & O'Connor Mortuary death records 1950-1978 (catalog 771104), and the Rose Hills database of burials from 1914 (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Los_Angeles_County,_California_Genealogy#Obituaries).
- **Browse-only volumes:** The survey counts 255 browse-only Death volumes for Los Angeles; these must be read image by image.
- **Adjoining counties:** Search Kern, Orange, San Bernardino and Ventura counties too, since a death near a county line may be filed across it (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Los_Angeles_County,_California_Genealogy).
- **Not established:** The survey does not place Kenneth Werner Quass's death in Los Angeles or anywhere else. The Find a Grave and Texas death certificate captures are not treated as the place of death.
